c01s03.title: One action, two explanations
c01s03.caption: The quick repair is observed. Experience and label use are competing explanations; the branches are hypotheses, not established causes.

c01s03b.title: Compare what each account predicts
c01s03b.caption: Familiarity and label usefulness should be varied in comparable tasks to distinguish their predictions.

c01s04.title: Faster can mean different things
c01s04.caption: Response time and accuracy must be interpreted together; the diagram shows possible accounts, not measured results.

c01s05.title: A useful measure has boundaries
c01s05.caption: Control can clarify a proposed process while reducing resemblance to everyday settings. Neither setting automatically settles the interpretation.

c02s03.title: An interpretation uses several cues
c02s03.caption: Sensory features and prior expectations both contribute to an interpretation. Their contributions are to be investigated, not read directly from confidence.

c02s03b.title: Same mark, different context
c02s03b.caption: Context can favor different readings of an ambiguous mark. Improving the signal supplies evidence beyond the first expectation.

c02s04.title: Two decisions a test can confuse
c02s04.caption: More yes responses can reflect a changed criterion. Both signal-present and signal-absent trials are needed to interpret discrimination.

c02s05.title: Use the idea within its scope
items: A context effect in a task
c02s05.caption: A perceptual demonstration motivates a check; it does not show that every disagreement is an illusion.

c03s03.title: A goal selects information
c03s03.caption: Prioritizing the count can leave an unexpected arrival unreported. Visibility and other alternatives still need checking.

c03s03b.title: Test an attention account
c03s03b.caption: Vary the attention demand while keeping the arrival as comparable as possible. Expected arrivals create a different task from unexpected ones.

c03s04.title: An interruption changes the active goal
c03s04.caption: The sequence illustrates the need to resume a prior goal. It does not assign a fixed cost to every interruption.

c03s05.title: A miss does not identify a motive
c03s05.caption: A missed event can have several contributing processes. One miss is not a measure of care, intelligence or a general attentional capacity.

c04s03.title: Following instructions requires updating
c04s03.caption: Working memory supports maintaining and using information. Updating a sequence adds demands beyond hearing the words.

c04s03b.title: Knowledge changes the useful unit
c04s03b.caption: Chunking depends on learned meaning. The figure does not imply a fixed number of items for everyone.

c04s04.title: Change where the next step is stored
c04s04.caption: An external record changes the task’s internal memory demands. It must stay accurate and accessible.

c04s05.title: Keep the benefit claim specific
c04s05.caption: Improvement with a checklist or practice does not by itself establish a broad increase in working-memory capacity.

c05s03.title: A later explanation needs retrieval
c05s03.caption: The stages are useful distinctions, not a literal diagram of three isolated brain stores.

c05s03b.title: Attempt, inspect, correct
c05s03b.caption: Retrieval practice with feedback tests the later demand more directly than judging the familiarity of a visible page.

c05s04.title: Two changes in practice
c05s04.caption: Spacing concerns timing; interleaving concerns the arrangement of relevant material. They are different manipulations.

c05s05.title: Ease now and learning later
c05s05.caption: Immediate ease is not equivalent to durable learning. The comparison must match the goal and assessment.

c06s03.title: A remembered account has sources
c06s03.caption: Remembering can combine information from different sources. Reconstruction does not imply that all memories are false.

c06s03b.title: Where did the color detail come from?
c06s03b.caption: Source monitoring concerns the origin of a detail. An open question reduces one source of suggestion.

c06s04.title: Keep certainty and evidence distinct
c06s04.caption: Confidence may be informative under suitable procedures, but it is not an unrestricted guarantee of accuracy.

c06s05.title: A discrepancy permits several accounts
c06s05.caption: Neither a disagreement nor a memory label establishes a particular cause or deliberate dishonesty.

c07s03.title: A sentence uses several kinds of information
c07s03.caption: Knowing the words does not guarantee identifying the speaker’s intended referent in this context.

c07s03b.title: “The cabinet” can identify two places
c07s03b.caption: The same expression can be interpreted differently when speakers assume different common ground.

c07s04.title: A check-back exposes the interpretation
c07s04.caption: A specific comprehension check elicits the action or reference needed for the task. It is not a test of personal worth.

c07s05.title: Match the research to the claim
items: No single explanation for all gaps
c07s05.caption: Psycholinguistic tasks examine selected processes; an everyday communication difficulty can have several causes.

c08s03.title: A typical case is not a complete rule
c08s03.caption: Typicality can guide classification while concealing cases that differ from a familiar example.

c08s03b.title: Separate two repair rules
c08s03b.caption: Find a safe case where the accounts predict different results. Another matching example may not distinguish them.

c08s04.title: The wording opens or closes options
c08s04.caption: Changing the problem representation can reveal options without guaranteeing an insight or the correct solution.

c08s05.title: A fair test can change your view
c08s05.caption: A bias label cannot substitute for examining which alternatives were considered and which evidence discriminates.

c09s03.title: Vividness and frequency differ
c09s03.caption: A dramatic incident may deserve safety attention without being the most frequent kind of fault.

c09s03b.title: Positive results need the right group
c09s03b.caption: Invented teaching counts: ten faulty devices yield eight true positives; ninety without faults yield nine false positives. Eight of seventeen positive results are real faults.

c09s04.title: One change, two descriptions
c09s04.caption: These invented equivalent rates illustrate the importance of a starting value and shared denominator.

c09s05.title: A useful judgment includes consequences
c09s05.caption: A shortcut is not automatically irrational. Its usefulness depends on the task, available information and consequences.

c10s03.title: Monitoring can guide a next action
items: What do I think I know?
c10s03.caption: Metacognition includes both judgments about cognition and actions based on those judgments.

c10s03b.title: Test a confidence prediction
c10s03b.caption: Calibration requires comparing confidence with suitable performance, usually across several judgments.

c10s04.title: Build a bounded explanation
c10s04.caption: Use cognitive concepts to generate tests, rather than assigning a process label to every everyday mistake.

c10s05.title: A visit is not a mastery score
c10s05.caption: A delayed unfamiliar case is more informative than page visits or familiarity, while still not certifying general mastery.
